question: How does MSC 6.00AX (/AL) emit explicitly far data, and where do the bytes of a far variable come from?
findings: Initialised far data and static far data (initialised or not) of a file go to one segment <BASENAME><n>_DATA, class FAR_DATA, combine public, PARAGRAPH aligned; n is the SEGDEF index (7 with /Zi because $$SYMBOLS/$$TYPES take 5 and 6, 5 without).
Static uninitialised far arrays are laid out first (zeros), initialised definitions after them.
A public far variable without initialiser is a COMDEF far communal (no bytes in the object); the linker allocates it (FAR_BSS).

When the next item does not fit into 64K (exactly 0x10000 still fits: the SEGDEF then has the big bit and length 0), MSC closes the segment and opens <BASENAME><n+1>_DATA: with the real sizes this reproduces the 3E1D (0xF89F) / 4DA7 (0x900) frames of SIMANT.EXE.

Code of the defining file references its own far variables with fixup target = the SEGMENT, other files with target = the EXTERNAL symbol; RTLink groups relocations by target, so the defining file's references form one group (the ownership test of work/data/exclude.py).
positive_control: S23:39C7 UNIT7_DATA at 4EE5:0000 (placed, exact): its code relocations 97-102 to 4EE5 interleave fd_4EE5_0280/0000/0500 in one run in FIXUPP order; data:3E1D reproduces the 3E1D/4DA7 split byte for byte.
negative_contrast: root:1FD2 references 5071:03C4, 0728 and 0060 as externs: three separate relocation groups with a 50F6 group between them. In this probe: a tentative definition gives a communal and no segment bytes; without /Zi the segment is UNIT5_DATA; one byte more than 64K moves the next array into UNIT8_DATA.
